hypotheses.claim: H1. Task complexity, not model size, predicts fit for Vanguard tasks
hypotheses.measurement: Per-pillar score against parameter count and cost per task, with a complexity rating per task
hypotheses.confirmedIf: Most pillars plateau at a mid-size or small model class; score correlates with task complexity more than with model size
hypotheses.refutedIf: Scores keep rising with model size across most pillars, including bounded tasks

hypotheses.claim: H2. Frontier upgrades do not move Vanguard-relevant metrics
hypotheses.measurement: Re-run the full task library on each new frontier release and compare with the incumbent on the pillars we use
hypotheses.confirmedIf: Public benchmark gains are large while VAI pillar movement is within noise, except on named reasoning-heavy pillars
hypotheses.refutedIf: Each release moves several VAI pillars past the production bar where the incumbent fell short

hypotheses.claim: H3. Task-specific trained smaller models beat general models in Vanguard context
hypotheses.measurement: For each pillar, a fine-tuned or distilled specialist against the best general model at equal latency budget, with retraining cost included
hypotheses.confirmedIf: Specialists win on bounded pillars (1, 3-routing, 7, 14, 15) at lower cost, and the gap holds across two quarterly re-runs
hypotheses.refutedIf: General models match specialists at similar cost, or specialist gains erode between re-runs faster than retraining is affordable

portfolio.horizonMixNote: H1: VAI, self-healing. H2: VI Portal. H3: Think Latent (graduated, outside the lab). The active lab holds no H3 bet; acceptable for one quarter while VAI proves the core, to be revisited at the next review.
portfolio.diagnosis: The constraint on VI is not model quality but evidence for adoption and governance throughput: owned models exist, and nothing proves to the business and Risk that they are sufficient and safe for a given workflow. Ideas that relieve this constraint come first.

spine.winningAspiration: Every model decision at Vanguard runs on evidence, and most AI work runs on models Vanguard owns, inside its own boundary, at lower cost and with clearer governance than renting frontier models by default.
spine.whereToPlay: Bounded, high-volume workflows (extraction, classification, routing, servicing, compliance pre-review) on Vanguard-built specialists; frontier models only where measured evidence shows a gain worth paying for. Not: general-purpose chat products, or competing with vendors on frontier capability.
spine.howToWin: Evidence nobody else has (the index on Vanguard tasks), an owned build-and-heal loop (VGLM, compression, self-healing), and a governance path that approves usages faster than the side door.
spine.capabilitiesRequired: Evaluation register and harness; AI Gateway; HyperPod serving; compression pipeline; self-healing system; usage-approval record; contribution flow.
spine.managementSystems: The Vanguard AI Index and its quarterly report, the Idea Register, the governance loop on the portal, and this lab.
